issues.evidence: PCB: the AP3441 buck U3 sits at (138.0,72.9) on B.Cu, but its only /CM5_5V input caps (C6 10u, C7 10u, C8 100n) are at about (149-152.5, 87.6), roughly 17-18 mm from VIN pin 3. The output caps C10-C13 are close (about 5-10 mm).
issues.why_it_matters: A synchronous buck's input cap must close the VIN to PGND hot loop within a few mm. At 17 mm the loop inductance gives VIN/LX ringing and spikes, EMI, and possible instability or overstress of the 5.5 V-max AP3441 input.

issues.evidence: Label /PCIe_PWR_EN connects only to Conn2 pin 6. The M.2 3.3 V buck U3 EN instead comes from R9 100k to /CM5_5V, so it is always on.
issues.why_it_matters: The CM5 cannot power-cycle the M.2 SSD (OS control and recovery are lost). A dangling label usually means a missed connection.

issues.evidence: The /CM5_3V3 net (CM5 3.3 V output) has no capacitor at all. RT9742 load switch U1 IN (pin 5) and 74LVC1G07 U5 VCC (pin 5) have no local bypass. Only the In2 3V3 pour is present.
issues.why_it_matters: When U1 switches the SD card's inrush onto SD_PWR (C1 10u), the CM5's 3V3 output dips with nothing local to supply it. The RT9742 datasheet recommends an input cap at IN.

issues.evidence: USB-C VBUS (/USB_5V) feeds the CM5 5V input through jumper J5 with no fuse, TVS or reverse/overvoltage protection. CC uses only 5.1k Rd (R14/R15), so the board negotiates at most 5 V/3 A. The CM5 recommends a 5 V/5 A supply with peripherals.
issues.why_it_matters: Unprotected input feeding an expensive module. Possible brown-outs under an NVMe plus CM5 load.

issues.evidence: Each PCIe line changes from F.Cu (In1 GND reference) to B.Cu (In4 GND reference) through one via. The nearest GND via is 1.0-2.2 mm away (TX_P 2.2 mm, RX_N 1.9 mm).
issues.why_it_matters: Return current has to find a stitching path between the planes. A closer GND via (<1 mm) per pair is better practice at 5-8 GT/s. Probably tolerable for one short Gen2/3 x1 link.

issues.evidence: USB-C D+/D- (/USB2_P, /USB2_N) go straight to CM5 Conn2 with no ESD array. The Ethernet pairs do have CDDFN10 ESD arrays (U7/U8).
issues.why_it_matters: A user-touchable connector has an unprotected path to the CM5 SoC.

acceptable_designs.reason: PCIe data P/N are swapped (RX_N to J3 PETp0 pin 43, TX_N to PERp0 pin 49). Direction is correct (host RX to module PET). PCIe receivers must support lane polarity inversion, so this is legal and eases routing. REFCLK P/N are not swapped.
No PCIe AC-coupling caps on the carrier. The CM5 carries its own TX coupling caps and the M.2 SSD carries its own, per the Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5 carrier reference.
The CDDFN10-3324P (TPD4EUSB30-style) NC pins 6/7/9/10 tie onto the signal nets for flow-through routing.
3-pin jumper J5 deliberately selects the 5 V source (USB-C or PoE) for /CM5_5V. It does not short the supplies.
About 1.75 mm length difference (97.7 vs 99.4 mm), partly from the Type-C A/B row tie. That is about 11 ps, negligible at 480 Mbit/s. Vias are symmetric (3 each).
One set of 2.2k pull-ups to /CM5_3V3 on GPIO2/3 for the Qwiic port J6.
Every LED has a series resistor (R6/R7 470R for the MagJack LEDs, R3/R11/R12 1k). They are driven by active-low or open-drain sources.
R8 10k / R10 2.2k with 0.6 V Vref gives about 3.33 V for M.2. C9 4.7n is feed-forward. The AP3441 is rated 3 A.
SD_VDD_Override is deliberately strapped low through 1k (normal SD voltage switching).

[acceptable] J7 is the 4-pin JST-SH fan header (5V/PWM/GND/TACHO), a keyed output; /CM5_5V is fed through jumper J5 from USB_5V or PoE_5V, so it is not an unprotected power entry and a fan header needs no reverse/ESD part
[acceptable] Fact true (nearest GND via ~7.4 mm), but PCIe CLKREQ# is an open-drain low-speed sideband signal, not a differential lane; return-path via stitching is irrelevant

notes: Reviewed the netlist, the 6-layer PCB (In1/In4 GND planes, PCIe/USB/Ethernet lengths and vias, decoupling distances) and the custom footprint pad counts. Not verified: the MB6S and SMAJ58A pad-to-pin polarity in the custom footprints (pad numbers match the symbol, but the cathode mark was not checked); the RT9742GGJ5 enable polarity against the 12k pull-up R2 on SD_PWR_ON; the CM5 FAN_TACHO internal pull-up; and the purpose of R1 2.2k from /USB_5V to GND (a 2.3 mA bleeder, harmless). Impedance and stack-up not checked.
